headline: Walmart beat and raised again as U.S. comps rose 4.5%, with higher-income households driving most share gains.
guidance_note: FY26 sales growth raised to 4.8-5.1% cc (from 3.75-4.75%); adj. EPS to $2.58-2.63 (from $2.52-2.62).
key_messages: Walmart U.S. comp ex fuel +4.5% (transactions +1.8%, ticket +2.7%); U.S. eCommerce +28%, global +27%.
Sam's Club U.S. comp ex fuel +3.8%.
Households earning over $100K accounted for ~75% of share gains; lower-income families under added pressure.
Advertising up ~28%; eCommerce growth topped 20% for a 7th straight quarter.
Raised full-year sales and EPS outlook heading into the holidays.

consumer.income_split: Upper- and middle-income households drove growth; lower-income families under additional pressure.
consumer.quote: "Households earning more than $100,000 made up 75% of our share gains." - CEO Doug McMillon

macro_read: A K-shaped consumer: affluent shoppers trading into Walmart kept spending solid in late 2025 while lower-income households showed strain.

sources.label: Zacks: Walmart lifts FY26 outlook on Q3 beat

notes: Revenue and EPS consensus and the stock reaction were removed because they came from memory, not a confirmed source.
